hero.title: Virtual Nature Expedition: Exploring the Puger Ecosystem
hero.description: Behind the crashing waves and the mesmerizing sunsets of Puger Beach, lies a hidden secret that threatens our future. Through 360° exploration videos and augmented reality technology, let's go beyond the limits of sight to uncover how microplastic pollution infiltrates the food chain and affects human health. This beauty is ours, and so is our responsibility to protect it.

objectives.title: Learning Objectives
objectives.goal_1: After exploring environmental contamination through 360 Video and AR microplastic media, students are able to describe the systemic impact of microplastics on public health and ecosystems comprehensively and accurately
objectives.goal_2: Through interactive analysis of the 360 ​​video of the condition of the Puger TPI and AR visualization of microplastics, students are able to assess the complexity of the problem by integrating ecological, economic, and social aspects into a system relationship matrix (causal-loop) in a holistic and logical manner
objectives.goal_3: Based on a systemic understanding of the results of observations using 360 Video and AR microplastic, students are able to design strategic and innovative solution proposals for microplastic mitigation in the Jember region that meet the criteria for ecological, economic, and social balance in a sustainable manner
objectives.goal_4: After going through a series of 360 Video and AR-based learning experiences, students are able to formulate logical decisions to overcome the dilemma of plastic use in everyday life consistently and responsibly

mission.title: The Invisible Crisis
mission.subtitle: Microplastics in the Jember Ecosystem
mission.description: A multidisciplinary investigation into how urban plastic consumption patterns create a systemic threat extending 45 km to the Puger estuary.

context.p1: The problem begins when people's consumption patterns change There has been a drastic shift to single-use plastics, while the waste management system has not been able to keep up with the load. Plastic waste dumped into the <0>Bedadung River</0> in urban areas doesn't stay there.
context.p2: The river carries it 45 km to the Puger estuary. There, invisible particles infiltrate <0>the tissues of fish and shellfish</0>, posing a systemic threat to public health and the balance of Jember's interconnected ecosystem.

initial.instruction: Watch a 360° video of the port and interviews with three stakeholders (Seafarers, Seafood Vendors, and Government Officials).

tips.suffix: For a full 360° experience, click and drag the video screen to look around the TPI and see the perspectives of different stakeholders.

initial.description: With your group members, watch a 360-degree video of the Puger TPI area and listen to excerpts from interviews with local residents. Discuss your initial findings and agree on answers to the following questions:

sailor.label: Fishermen
sailor.summary: Complaining about piles of trash caught in their nets and boat engines.

seller.label: Seafood Seller
seller.summary: Concerned about the quality of fish contaminated by plastic waste at the port.

official.label: Government Official
official.summary: Explaining the difficulties of waste management regulations in coastal areas.

initial.issue_description: After watching the video and listening to the interview, what are the most pressing issues? Why are these issues interconnected between fishermen, fish sellers, and the government?

component_ecosystem.title: Identifying Ecosystem Components
component_ecosystem.description: Identify at least 5 components (biotic and abiotic). Use the table feature to group them: Components, Types, and Roles (Source of Pollutant/Victim/Medium of Transportation).
component_ecosystem.question: How do you connect the accumulation of plastic waste seen in the video to the potential unseen biological threats to marine life?

table_component.role_placeholder: Source of Pollutant, Victim, Medium of Transportation

initial.source_question: Based on the video, where are the main sources of plastic waste that has the potential to enter and settle in the waters of the Puger TPI?
initial.awareness_question: Based on the interview results, what is the level of awareness of local communities regarding the dangers of invisible plastics (microplastics)? What social barriers have been identified?
initial.footer: Ensure all component and property observations are filled in before proceeding to the analysis phase.

qualitative.instruction: Compare the large plastic bottles (seen at the port) with the microplastic fibers (mentioned by the seller).

analysis.q1_desc: Have an in-depth discussion with your group mates and make a qualitative prediction chart regarding the pathway of change of how macro plastic waste (bottles/nets) is fragmented into microplastics.
analysis.q2_desc: Plastic waste floating in Puger waters undergoes degradation. Its surface is rapidly colonized by bacteria, microalgae, and pathogens, forming a mini-ecosystem called the "Plastisphere." Furthermore, biofouling by algae produces the compound Dimethyl sulfide (DMS).
analysis.q2_step1: Create a qualitative diagram showing the path of marine plastic fragmentation to form the Plastisphere ecosystem.
analysis.q2_step2: Analyze how the formation of the Plastisphere and the release of DMS gas affect the foraging behavior of endemic/local marine animals (such as pelagic seabirds or reef fish).
analysis.q2_step3: Why do these biological changes on the plastic surface qualitatively increase the risk of microplastics being actively ingested by marine animals (rather than just accidentally)?

qualitative.footer: This qualitative analysis will form the basis for quantitative calculations in the next phase.

diagram_input.hints: Drag the circle on the edge of a variable to another variable to establish a causal relationship.

quantitative.instruction: In the qualitative section, you analyzed how microplastics, when left in water for extended periods, form a plastisphere and release DMS gas, which triggers active ingestion by marine animals. Now, analyze the following field data from the Bedadung watershed to the Puger coast to demonstrate the systemic impact of this phenomenon.

abundance.title: Microplastic Abundance Analysis (Spatial)
abundance.description: Examine the two quantitative data tables in your worksheet. Collaboratively discuss any patterns, anomalies, or spikes in the data with your group. Answer the following questions based on the results of your group's mathematical analysis:

biomagnification.title: Trophic Level & Biomagnification
biomagnification.description: Researchers extracted digestive and muscle tissue from various organisms in the Puger Marine Zone to examine the transfer of microplastics through food webs.

questions.q1_desc: Why did the concentration decrease at Station 4 but increase sharply at Station 3? This is attributed to the breakdown of microplastics and the formation of plastipheres.
questions.q2_desc: Based on data from Station 2, calculate the estimated number of microplastic particles ingested by humans if they use water from the river body (without RO filtration) as much as 2 liters per day!
questions.q3_desc: Calculate the Biomagnification Factor (BMF) from Marine Phytoplankton to Blood Cockles (passive ingestion/filter feeding), then compare it with the BMF from Blood Cockles to Indian Mackerel. Use your qualitative understanding of DMS gas to explain why there was such an extreme spike in plastic accumulation in Indian Mackerel (a pelagic fish that hunts using olfactory chemosensory signals)!
questions.q4_desc: How does active ingestion at the secondary consumer level (Mackerel) accelerate the biomagnification process to reach 48.50 mg/kg in Yellowfin Tuna?
questions.q5_desc: If a local resident consumes 250 grams of Blood Cockles per week from these waters, how many milligrams total mass of plastic that enters his digestive system in one month?

explanation.instruction: Open the Augmented Reality (AR) app on your device. Focus on the "Mobile Impact" and "Fragmentation" modules.

setup.title: Augmented Reality (AR) User Guide
step: Make sure you're using an Android-based device (smartphone). Scan the following QR code to download the AR app (this app is guaranteed safe for your device).
Once downloaded, install and open the app.
Please read the User Guide available within the app.
Select (tap) one of the Scenes, then point your device's camera at the Marker image displayed on the web page.
Have fun exploring and enjoying the AR experience!

explanation.guide: Use each member's smartphone to scan the AR marker Fragmentation & Human Health Risk. Specifically observe Scenes 2 and 3. Afterward, brainstorm within the group to map this systemic crisis:

question.estimation_physical_factor: Based on observations of Scenes 2-3 in the AR app, how long do you estimate it will take for macroplastic waste to fully fragment into microplastics in the Puger marine environment? What physical factors accelerate this process?
question.human_digestion: Biochemically, why are these microplastics recalcitrant (unable to be digested or broken down) by enzymes or stomach acid in the human digestive system?
question.health_impact: Based on the visualization of the microplastic entry route into vital human organs in the AR app, explain the systemic health impacts that can occur from consuming contaminated seafood over a long period of time!

causal_loop.title: Causal Loop Diagram
causal_loop.desc: Construct a causal loop diagram connecting all the subsystems you have studied. Ensure your diagram includes the interaction flow between the following elements: (Social/Tourism): Waste disposal activities in the upstream, market, and coastal areas of Puger
point: (Micro-Ecology-AR): Plastic fragmentation process in the Puger marine zone.
(Biology/Chemo-sensory): Plastisphere Formation & DMS Gas Release (Based on Phase 2)
(Behavior & Ecotoxicology): Active Ingestion & Extreme Biomagnification processes in the Puger Food Web (Based on Phase 3 Data)
(Human Health-AR): Particle Entry Routes & Systemic Health Impacts on Human Organs.
(Macro-Impacts): Long-term consequences on the Fishermen's Economy (decrease in catch quality) and widespread ecosystem damage.

decision.instruction: As a team of scientists, discuss within your group. Debate scientifically to select, evaluate, and agree on the most rational final mitigation solution to be implemented in the Puger area. Based on the critical points in your group's Causal Loop Diagram, propose one specific strategy (applied technology, biological monitoring, or ecological intervention) to address this problem!

ecology_biosafety.title: Ecological & Biosafety Parameters
ecology_biosafety.description: Does your biological solution pose any side risks to the native Puger ecosystem? (For example, concerns about the release of GMOs or alien species).

fisherman_economy.title: Fisherman's Economic Parameters
fisherman_economy.description: Will implementing this strategy financially burden local fishermen, or will it save the Puger fish market in the long run?

economy_impact.title: Fisherman's Economic Parameters
economy_impact.description: Will implementing this strategy financially burden local fishermen, or will it save the Puger fish market in the long run?

env_impact.title: Ecological Parameters & Biosafety
env_impact.description: Does your biological solution pose any side effects to the native Puger ecosystem? (E.g., concerns about the release of GMOs or alien species)

conclusion.title: Professional Conclusion
conclusion.desc_primary: Instructions for Presentation & Class Discussion (Defending an Argument):
conclusion.desc: At the end of this phase, each group will present the results of their discussion to the class. You do not need to create a new copy of the presentation (such as PowerPoint). Project your group's LKM web dashboard directly onto the classroom screen as the main presentation medium!
conclusion.presenter_desc: Defend the feasibility of your group's solution (scientific defense). Re-display the data graphs or analysis on your website if needed to answer questions from lecturer or other groups.
conclusion.audience_desc: Be a critical reviewer of the group presenting. Listen carefully and provide high-level questions (HOTS) or constructive criticism regarding gaps in the ecological solutions they propose.
